question: Miki has a dozen oranges of the same size and a dozen pears of the same size. Miki uses her juicer to extract \(8\) ounces of pear juice from \(3\) pears and \(8\) ounces of orange juice from \(2\) oranges. She makes a pear-orange juice blend from an equal number of pears and oranges. What percent of the blend is pear juice?
solution:
Changing the positive equal number of pears and oranges multiplies both juice amounts by the same factor, so it leaves the pear percentage unchanged. We can therefore calculate using all twelve of each fruit. Twelve pears make four groups of three, yielding \(4\cdot8=32\) ounces of pear juice. Twelve oranges make six groups of two, yielding \(6\cdot8=48\) ounces of orange juice. The blend contains \(32+48=80\) ounces, so its pear percentage is
\[
\frac{32}{80}\cdot100\%=40\%.
\]
The answer is \(\text{B}\).
